title: Cyclotomic character values and reduction to the prime-to-p part
statement: Let $N\geq1$, let $\zeta\in\mathbf C$ be a primitive $N$th root of unity, let $K=\mathbf Q(\zeta)\subset\mathbf C$, and let $A\subset K$ consist of the elements satisfying a monic polynomial in $\mathbf Z[T]$. Let $G$ be a finite group with $|G|$ dividing $N$, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space with an action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbf C}(V)$. Put $\chi_V(g)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf C}(\rho(g))$. Then $\chi_V(g)\in A$ for every $g\in G$. Furthermore let $p$ be any prime, $k$ any field of characteristic $p$, and $r:A\to k$ any unital ring homomorphism. If $g=su$ with $s,u\in G$ commuting, the order of $s$ prime to $p$ and the order of $u$ a power of $p$ (including $1$), then $r(\chi_V(g))=r(\chi_V(s))$. Such $s,u$, both powers of $g$, exist for every $g\in G$. Here field generation is [def-weil-simple-field-extension], $A$ is the integral closure of $\mathbf Z$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and finite-dimensional means having a finite spanning family [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace].

proof.text: First fix any abelian subgroup $H\leq G$. The field $\mathbf C$ is algebraically closed by [lem-weil-complex-algebraically-closed] and has characteristic zero. Apply [lem-per-finite-group-character-decomposition] to $V|_H$, obtaining a finite direct sum of nonzero irreducible $H$-representations $W_j$ (the sum is empty if $V=0$). For each $W_j$ apply [lem-per-normal-commuting-weight-induction] with its finite group equal to $H$ and its normal subgroup also equal to $H$. Its commuting-image hypothesis holds because $H$ is abelian. Conjugation in $H$ fixes every character of $H$, so the transitive action on the nonempty set $X$ in that statement forces $X$ to have one element. Thus $H$ acts by a single character $\lambda_j:H\to\mathbf C^\times$ on all of $W_j$. Choose a finite basis of each $W_j$: projections of a finite spanning family of $V$ span the summands, and deleting dependent entries gives bases. Their union, transported through the direct-sum isomorphism, is a basis of $V$ consisting of common eigenvectors for $H$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace, def-weil-pbc-free-module]. This is a direct specialization of the two cited representation statements.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-finite-additive-group-card-annihilator] on the group $G$ written additively (no commutativity is required): its formula becomes $h^{|G|}=1$ for every $h\in G$. Since $|G|\mid N$, also $h^N=1$. The $N$ powers $1,\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^{N-1}$ are distinct: equality with exponents $0\leq i<j<N$ gives $\zeta^{j-i}=1$, contradicting primitivity. They all belong to $\mu_N(\mathbf C)$, whose cardinality is at most $N$ by [lem-exc-field-roots-cyclic-bound]. Hence every complex $N$th root of unity is one of these powers. Each lies in $K$ by [def-weil-simple-field-extension] and is integral over $\mathbf Z$, being a root of the monic polynomial $T^N-1$; therefore it lies in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For arbitrary $h\in G$, use Step 1 for the abelian cyclic subgroup $\langle h\rangle$. Write its eigenvalues, with repetitions, as $a_1,\ldots,a_t$. Applying $\rho(h)^N=1$ to each nonzero basis vector gives $a_i^N=1$, so $a_i\in A$. The trace formula [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] gives $\chi_V(h)=\sum_i a_i$. The subring assertion in [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] gives $\chi_V(h)\in A$, also for the empty sum.

proof.text:
Take any decomposition $g=su$ satisfying the hypotheses, and write $u^{p^a}=1$ with $a\geq0$. The subgroup $H=\langle s,u\rangle$ is abelian: every word can be reordered into $s^b u^c$ with integer exponents. Apply Step 1 to $H$. In its common eigenbasis let $\alpha_i,\beta_i$ be the respective eigenvalues of $s,u$. Step 2 gives $s^N=u^N=1$, whence $\alpha_i^N=\beta_i^N=1$ and $\alpha_i,\beta_i\in A$. Moreover $\beta_i^{p^a}=1$. Put $b_i=r(\beta_i)$. The iterate of Frobenius on $k$ is a ring endomorphism sending $x$ to $x^{p^a}$ by [def-weil-ring-frobenius], so $(b_i-1)^{p^a}=b_i^{p^a}-1=r(\beta_i^{p^a})-1=0$. Since $k$ is a field and $p^a>0$, a nonzero $b_i-1$ would have a nonzero power; thus $b_i=1$. On each basis vector $\rho(su)$ acts by $\alpha_i\beta_i$, so [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] and the homomorphism laws give
$$r(\chi_V(g))=\sum_i r(\alpha_i)r(\beta_i)=\sum_i r(\alpha_i)=r(\chi_V(s)).$$
This proves the reduction for every commuting pair in the statement, without assuming that the pair consists of powers of $g$.

proof.text: It remains to construct a pair. Write $|G|=p^a d$ with $a\geq0$ and $p\nmid d$, by repeatedly dividing the positive integer $|G|$ by $p$ as long as possible. Regard the cyclic subgroup $C=\langle g\rangle$ additively as a $\mathbf Z$-module, with integer scalar multiplication given in multiplicative notation by integer powers. Step 2 shows that every element of $C$ is killed by $|G|$. The integers $p^a,d$ are coprime, including $a=0$ or $d=1$. Apply [lem-sc-coprime-torsion-decomposition] with $R=\mathbf Z$, $M=C$, two indices, and $q_1=d$, $q_2=p^a$. Its product-annihilator hypothesis is exactly the preceding assertion. The internal direct sum gives $g=s+u$ with $ds=0$ and $p^a u=0$; its two components have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. In multiplicative notation $g=su$, $s^d=1$, and $u^{p^a}=1$. Their orders divide $d$ and $p^a$, respectively: division of an annihilating positive exponent by the least positive order leaves a smaller annihilating remainder, which must be zero. Thus the order of $s$ is prime to $p$, and that of $u$ is a power of $p$, possibly $1$. Both are in $C$, so they are integer powers of $g$ and commute. Reducing these integer exponents modulo $|G|$, using $g^{|G|}=1$, also expresses both as nonnegative powers of $g$.

tool_uses.why: The usual complex coefficient field satisfies the algebraic-closure hypothesis of the representation statements; a generic field fact.
Renaming multiplication as addition gives the exponent bound for the finite group; the statement expressly permits noncommutative groups.
The root-count bound exhausts the Nth roots by powers of the specified primitive root. This avoids any characteristic-zero ambiguity in lem-sc-primitive-root.
The Z-module underlying the cyclic subgroup supplies the two commuting powers with the required annihilating exponents; a generic tool, not a replacement of a unit step.
Its statement includes the ring-endomorphism property of every iterate, giving the power-of-a-difference identity in the residue field.
Its statement explicitly includes the subring theorem for integral elements, Stacks 00GO, not merely the construction.
The sum of diagonal entries in its statement is used in the common eigenbasis.
